report.tagline: America's largest app-only bank brand, offering fee-free checking, early paychecks and small fee-free overdrafts to everyday workers.
report.simpleSummary: Chime is a bank account that lives on your phone. There are no monthly fees or overdraft fees, and your paycheck can arrive up to two days early. If you run short, SpotMe covers you for up to $200 without a fee, and MyPay lets you get part of your pay before payday. Chime makes most of its money when you swipe its debit card, because stores pay a small fee on each swipe.

overview.whatItDoes: Chime offers checking and savings accounts, a Visa debit card, a secured credit card to build credit (Credit Builder), fee-free overdraft (SpotMe) and pay advances (MyPay). It is not itself a bank; accounts are held at partner banks like The Bancorp and Stride Bank. It serves people earning under about $100,000 who are tired of bank fees.
howItWorks: You open an account in the app in minutes with no minimum balance and no credit check.
You set up direct deposit, and your paycheck can arrive up to two days early.
You spend with the Chime Visa debit card; the store's bank pays a small interchange fee that goes mostly to Chime.
SpotMe lets eligible members overdraw up to $200 with no fee.
MyPay gives up to $500 of earned pay before payday: free if you wait about a day, small fee for instant.
Members with bigger deposits join tiers like Chime Plus and Prime for cash back and higher savings rates.
overview.valueProposition: For members: a bank that does not punish you with fees when money is tight. For Chime: millions of members swiping their debit card for everyday spending, which earns interchange.

businessModel.summary: Chime gives banking for free and earns mostly from interchange on debit card swipes, plus fees from instant MyPay advances and other services.

revenueStreams.detail: Fees paid by stores on debit and Credit Builder card swipes; the largest part of revenue.
Small fee for instant pay advances; growing fast.
Fees for some ATM use and cash deposits at retailers.
Interest from partner banks and value from premium tiers.
Services for employers offering Chime to workers.

businessModel.pricing: Checking and savings: no monthly fees, no minimum balance. SpotMe: free (optional tips). MyPay: free with about a 24-hour wait, small fee (a few dollars) for instant. Out-of-network ATM: about $2.50. Chime Plus and Prime: free tiers based on direct deposit amount.
costDrivers: Partner bank fees and card processing
Fraud and losses on SpotMe and MyPay
businessModel.unitEconomics: Chime's average revenue per active member was about $250 a year in 2025. Most of that is interchange: a member who spends $1,500 a month on the debit card earns Chime about $20 to $25 a month, because small partner banks can charge higher swipe fees than big banks. Each member costs a few hundred dollars to win through ads, so Chime needs members to stay for a few years and move their paycheck in.

howTheyGetUsers: TV, sports and social ads about no fees
whatBringsUsersBack: SpotMe limits that grow with use
growth.moat: Chime's moat is its brand of 'no fees' with everyday workers, plus deposit data that lets it offer SpotMe and MyPay safely. Moving a paycheck is a hassle, so members who switch tend to stay.

pmLessons: Removing a hated fee can be the whole brand: 'no overdraft fees' built Chime.
Free products still need a money engine; for Chime it is interchange on card swipes.
Getting a user's paycheck is the most valuable step in banking.
Lending products like MyPay can turn a loss-making fintech profitable, but need careful risk control.
